tip: Past-tense verbs agree with the speaker's gender: a woman says читала (chitala = read), a man says читал (chital).
Motion toward uses на (na) plus accusative: пришла на работу (prishla na rabotu = came to work); staying there is на работе (na rabote).
пока (poka = while) pairs with imperfective verbs for two things at once: ждал (zhdal = was waiting), читал (chital = was reading).
Quantity words take the genitive: столько хлеба (stolko khleba = so much bread), not the plain form хлеб (khleb).
который (kotoryy = who) takes its gender from человека (cheloveka = person) but its case from its own clause, here subject, so nominative.
купил (kupil) is perfective, a finished one-time buy; imperfective покупал (pokupal) would mean was buying or used to buy.
Neuter subjects take было in the past: задание было (zadanie bylo = the assignment was); masculine был (byl), feminine была (byla).
Negation stacks in Russian: никогда (nikogda = never) still needs не (ne) before the verb, никогда не были (nikogda ne byli = have never been).
назад (nazad = ago) comes after the time span: две недели назад (dve nedeli nazad = two weeks ago), never before it.
о (o) becomes об (ob) before a vowel sound: об этом (ob etom = about this), but о книге (o knige = about a book).
Passive past uses был (byl) plus a short participle: был основан (byl osnovan = was founded).
The prefix в- (v-) adds inward motion: вошёл (voshyol = went in), while plain шёл (shyol) just means was walking.
кроме (krome = besides) takes the genitive: кроме тебя (krome tebya = besides you).
из (iz = out of) takes the genitive and matches the вы- (vy-) prefix: вышел из дома (vyshel iz doma = went out of the house).
к (k = toward) takes the dative: подошёл к окну (podoshyol k oknu = came up to the window).
из-за (iz-za = because of) takes the genitive and marks a negative cause: из-за дождя (iz-za dozhdya = because of the rain).
нужен (nuzhen) agrees with the needed noun, not the person: прогулка (progulka, feminine) takes нужна (nuzhna = is needed).
The one who likes goes dative: коту (kotu = to the cat). The verb agrees with the liked thing: нравится (nravitsya = likes, singular).
стать (stat' = to become) takes the instrumental: стала учительницей (stala uchitel'nitsey = became a teacher).
друг другу (drug drugu = each other) is fixed; only the second word shifts case, here dative after помогают (pomogayut = help).
Difficulty puts the person in the dative with no subject 'it': мне трудно (mne trudno = it is hard for me).
бывает (byvaet = tends to be) marks a recurring trait and takes an instrumental complement: холодной (kholodnoy = cold).
Russian places things with posture verbs: стол стоит (stol stoit = the table stands), not a plain 'is'.
между (mezhdu = between) takes the instrumental: между друзьями (mezhdu druz'yami = between friends).
среди (sredi = among) takes the genitive: среди гостей (sredi gostey = among the guests).
из also means made of, with the genitive: букет из роз (buket iz roz = a bouquet of roses).
нечего (nechego) plus an infinitive means having nothing to: нечего надеть (nechego nadet' = nothing to wear); the person goes dative, мне (mne).
Part-words take the genitive: часть денег (chast' deneg = part of the money), and ушла (ushla) agrees feminine with часть.
